P_MACRO_01_colonization_diversification_.result: 36/38 sampled Japanese species are in one dominant radiation while rare exceptional histories remain
P_MACRO_01_colonization_diversification_.why_problem: arrival count is not equivalent to diversification success

P_MACRO_02_topology_direction_identifiab.result: 270/945 rooted resolutions require regain; the rest permit a no-regain optimum
P_MACRO_02_topology_direction_identifiab.why_problem: directional trait-history claims depend on topology support, not phenotype coding alone

P_MACRO_03_species_tip_state_aggregation.basis: EAzami colour atlas + preliminary Fitch screen
P_MACRO_03_species_tip_state_aggregation.result: reviewed source-backed polymorphic taxon records=4; takaoense sample states W=3 C=3
P_MACRO_03_species_tip_state_aggregation.why_problem: one-state-per-species coding can erase within-lineage transitions

P_MACRO_04_evidence_nonindependence.result: published rows=4 but independent published data-generation groups=3
P_MACRO_04_evidence_nonindependence.why_problem: paper counts and accession rows can overstate independent replication

P_MACRO_05_phenotype_mechanism_scale_gap.basis: EAzami source-backed colour atlas + molecular literature
P_MACRO_05_phenotype_mechanism_scale_gap.result: white/polymorphic states occur across 5 reviewed phylogeny-context labels, while causal molecular mechanisms are not comparably resolved across those lineages
P_MACRO_05_phenotype_mechanism_scale_gap.why_problem: phenotypic convergence can be strong even when molecular convergence is unknown or heterogeneous

P_MACRO_06_species_mean_scale_compressio.result: Across nine image-derived endpoints, at least about half of visible variance remains below assigned-species means under photo-balance sensitivities, while precision-aware variation-vs-climate association is near zero (rho=-0.0569; hierarchical b=-0.0416, P=0.732).
P_MACRO_06_species_mean_scale_compressio.why_problem: species means and a single trait-lability axis collapse distinct within-species, environment-association, and macroevolutionary scales

P_MICRO_MACRO_07_annotation_to_orthology.basis: EAzami molecular coverage + public genome annotation + sequence-homology screens
P_MICRO_MACRO_07_annotation_to_orthology.why_problem: The apparent molecular gap changes qualitatively with evidence resolution: absence from a named pathway panel, absence of functional labels in distributed genome files, and absence of sequence homologs are not equivalent observations.

HMM1.name: latent-pathway / regulatory reversibility
HMM1.prediction: recent independent white lineages often retain structural flavonoid machinery and differ at regulatory/expression nodes more often than by shared destructive pathway loss
HMM1.falsifier: multiple well-resolved recent white lineages independently show irreversible loss/disruption of core pathway genes with no retained functional route

HMM2.name: population-aware transition-rate inflation relative to species-tip coding
HMM2.prediction: population/sample-aware coding yields more and younger W<->C transitions than one-state-per-species coding across replicated polymorphic systems
HMM2.falsifier: after topology uncertainty is propagated, population-aware coding does not increase transition count or shifts only one idiosyncratic system

HMM3.name: radiation-success / evolvability
HMM3.prediction: the dominant Japanese radiation shows higher genomic discordance/reticulation and-or faster trait or niche diversification than secondary histories after age and sampling controls
HMM3.falsifier: secondary histories show comparable evolvability metrics and diversification after age/sampling correction, leaving colonization timing/opportunity sufficient

HMM4.name: reticulation-phenotypic-transition coupling
HMM4.prediction: lineage-level gene-tree/cytonuclear discordance and ploidy/genome-size shifts positively covary with population-aware floral transition density
HMM4.falsifier: transition density is unrelated or negatively related to discordance across supported topology ensembles and leave-one-clade-out analyses

HMM5.name: phenotypic convergence / molecular heterogeneity
HMM5.prediction: convergence is stronger at phenotype/pathway/module level than at exact gene/nucleotide level across independent white systems
HMM5.falsifier: the same causal gene and homologous mutation class repeatedly explains independent white systems more strongly than module-level heterogeneity

HMM6.name: cross-scale trait decoupling
HMM6.prediction: after measurement and topology uncertainty are propagated, within-species visible dispersion, population-aware discrete transition density, within-species environment-trait association, and among-species niche/trait divergence remain only partially coupled rather than collapsing to one universal lability axis
HMM6.falsifier: validated cross-trait analyses recover a strong, consistent mapping from within-species dispersion to population transition density and among-species ecological/phylogenetic divergence across modules and clades

claim_boundary: Published conclusions, EAzami reanalyses, and own preliminary results remain separate. v3 adds a molecular resolution ladder but does not change HMM1-HMM6 provenance. A targeted-panel omission, missing functional annotation label, BLAST homology candidate, validated ortholog, functional gene, and causal colour-transition locus are distinct evidence levels and must not be collapsed.

own_preliminary_macro_trait_result.allowed_interpretation: Across the current image-derived endpoints, large visible variation below assigned-species means persists under photo-balance sensitivities, while no common cross-module coupling with within-species spatial climatic association remains after slope uncertainty is modelled.

molecular_resolution_ladder.named_targeted_panel: terminal anthocyanin + MBW + transport direct named coverage 0/7
molecular_resolution_ladder.distributed_genome_text_annotation: 0/13 requested functional term groups, including positive-control CHS/FLS/DFR; file exposes structural IDs rather than functional product labels
molecular_resolution_ladder.sequence_homology: 11/11 reviewed query anchors recover at least one C. nipponicum candidate homolog under frozen BLASTP settings
molecular_resolution_ladder.orthology_function: not yet established; enzyme and large-family candidates require domain/clade/reciprocal validation
molecular_resolution_ladder.colour_lineage_causation: not yet tested; candidates must be compared across morph-linked W/C lineages and against genome-wide ancestry/expression/pigment evidence

HMM1.what_changed: Existing-data analysis now recovers Cirsium genome candidates for DFR, ANS and all seven previously unlabelled terminal/regulatory/transport query families. This makes retained machinery testable and argues against treating reporting/annotation gaps as pathway loss, but it does not show that a white lineage retains functional copies or that regulation caused white colour.
HMM1.next_falsification_gate: validate candidate orthology/domain architecture, then test structural integrity/coding/expression in morph-linked white versus coloured lineages

HMM2.what_changed: 4/4 reviewed polymorphic systems expose state compression; 1/1 currently morph-linked system increases minimum count from 1 to 2; 0/4 support a replicated branch-length transition-rate comparison.
HMM2.next_falsification_gate: recover or generate morph-linked population genealogies for at least two additional polymorphic systems

HMM5.what_changed: Candidate homologs are recoverable for terminal, regulatory and transport families, enabling gene/module-level comparisons; no replicated white-lineage mechanism set exists yet.
HMM5.next_falsification_gate: validate ortholog/clade assignments and compare independent white systems at nucleotide, gene, module and pathway levels
